last.verdict: Investors sold the stock despite a delivery raise, focusing on cash burn and weak car margins.

reasons.label: Cars still lose money
reasons.text: Automotive gross profit stayed negative at $(36) million, helped by $108 million of regulatory credits.

reasons.label: R2 launch costs
reasons.text: R2 ramp added about $100 million in costs; free cash flow was $(849) million.

reasons.label: Dilution and funding needs
reasons.text: July's $1.3 billion share sale, plus more outside capital needed for the Georgia plant, weighed on the stock.

story: Rivian jumped about 27% in February on 2026 delivery guidance of 62,000-67,000 vehicles and the R2 launch. It slipped after the April report as car margins turned negative. Guidance has since been raised to 65,000-70,000, but costs and cash burn keep weighing.
